phy-910-01.heading: Physical quantities
phy-910-01.text: Anything that can be measured is a physical quantity. Quantities that do not depend on any other quantity — length, mass, time, temperature, electric current, luminous intensity and amount of substance — are fundamental quantities. Quantities derived from them, such as velocity, force and density, are derived quantities.

phy-910-01.heading: SI units
phy-910-01.text: The International System of Units (SI) has seven base units: metre (m) for length, kilogram (kg) for mass, second (s) for time, kelvin (K) for temperature, ampere (A) for electric current, candela (cd) for luminous intensity and mole (mol) for amount of substance.

phy-910-01.heading: Measuring instruments
phy-910-01.text: A metre scale measures to 1 mm. A slide calipers uses a vernier scale to measure to 0.1 mm or better. A screw gauge measures small thicknesses such as the diameter of a wire to 0.01 mm. Least count is the smallest value an instrument can measure.

phy-910-01.heading: Errors in measurement
phy-910-01.text: Systematic errors (for example zero error of an instrument) shift every reading the same way and can be corrected. Random errors vary from reading to reading and are reduced by taking several readings and using their average.

phy-910-02.heading: Rest and motion
phy-910-02.text: An object is in motion if its position changes with time relative to a reference point, and at rest if it does not. Rest and motion are therefore relative.

phy-910-02.heading: Speed and velocity
phy-910-02.text: Speed is distance travelled per unit time and is a scalar. Velocity is displacement per unit time and is a vector, so it has direction. Both are measured in metres per second (m/s).

phy-910-02.heading: Acceleration
phy-910-02.text: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v − u) / t. Its SI unit is m/s². A negative acceleration (slowing down) is called retardation.

phy-910-02.heading: Equations of motion
phy-910-02.text: For uniform acceleration: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², and v² = u² + 2as. A freely falling body near Earth accelerates at about g = 9.8 m/s².

phy-910-03.heading: What is force?
phy-910-03.text: A force is a push or a pull that changes, or tends to change, the state of rest or motion of an object. Its SI unit is the newton (N). One newton gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².

phy-910-03.heading: Newton's first law and inertia
phy-910-03.text: An object stays at rest, or keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless an unbalanced force acts on it. This tendency to resist a change in motion is inertia, and it depends on mass.

phy-910-03.heading: Newton's second law and momentum
phy-910-03.text: Momentum is mass × velocity (p = mv), measured in kg·m/s. The rate of change of momentum equals the applied force, which gives F = ma.

phy-910-03.heading: Newton's third law
phy-910-03.text: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. The two forces act on different bodies, so they never cancel each other. A rocket moves forward because it pushes exhaust gases backward.

phy-910-03.heading: Friction
phy-910-03.text: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact. Static friction is greater than sliding friction, which is greater than rolling friction — that is why wheels and ball bearings reduce friction.

phy-910-11.heading: Electric current
phy-910-11.text: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q / t. Its SI unit is the ampere (A); one ampere is one coulomb of charge passing a point each second. Current is measured with an ammeter connected in series.

phy-910-11.heading: Potential difference
phy-910-11.text: Potential difference is the work done in moving one coulomb of charge between two points. Its unit is the volt (V) and it is measured with a voltmeter connected in parallel.

phy-910-11.heading: Ohm's law and resistance
phy-910-11.text: At constant temperature, the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it: V = IR. R is resistance, measured in ohms (Ω). Resistance increases with the length of a wire and decreases with its cross-sectional area.

phy-910-11.heading: Series and parallel circuits
phy-910-11.text: In series, the same current flows through every resistor and R = R₁ + R₂ + … . In parallel, every resistor has the same voltage and 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + … , so the total resistance is less than the smallest resistor.

phy-910-11.heading: Electric power and energy
phy-910-11.text: Electric power P = VI, measured in watts (W). Energy used = power × time. Electricity bills use the kilowatt-hour (kWh): 1 kWh is 1000 W used for one hour, often called one "unit".

bio-910-02.heading: The cell
bio-910-02.text: The cell is the structural and functional unit of life. Prokaryotic cells (like bacteria) have no true nucleus, while eukaryotic cells (plants and animals) have a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

bio-910-02.heading: Mitochondria
bio-910-02.text: Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell. They carry out aerobic respiration and release energy stored in food as ATP, which the cell uses for its many activities. They have a double membrane and their own DNA.

bio-910-02.heading: Plastids and chloroplast
bio-910-02.text: Plastids are found in plant cells. Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, chromoplasts give colour to flowers and fruits, and leucoplasts store food.

bio-910-02.heading: Nucleus
bio-910-02.text: The nucleus controls all activities of the cell. It contains chromosomes made of DNA, which carry hereditary information, and a nucleolus that helps make ribosomes.

bio-910-02.heading: Other organelles
bio-910-02.text: Ribosomes make proteins. The endoplasmic reticulum transports materials. Golgi bodies package and secrete substances. Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes. Plant cells also have a cellulose cell wall and a large central vacuole, which animal cells lack.

bio-910-03.heading: Why cells divide
bio-910-03.text: Cells divide so that organisms can grow, replace worn-out cells and reproduce. The three types are amitosis, mitosis and meiosis.

bio-910-03.heading: Mitosis
bio-910-03.text: In mitosis one cell divides into two daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent. Its stages are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. It occurs in body (somatic) cells and drives growth.

bio-910-03.heading: Meiosis
bio-910-03.text: Meiosis takes place in reproductive cells. One cell divides twice to form four cells, each with half the chromosome number. This keeps chromosome number constant across generations and creates variation.

chem-910-03.heading: Atoms and subatomic particles
chem-910-03.text: An atom has a nucleus containing protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral), with electrons (negative) moving around it. In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

chem-910-03.heading: Atomic number and mass number
chem-910-03.text: Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons. Mass number (A) is protons plus neutrons. Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers, such as carbon-12 and carbon-14.

chem-910-03.heading: Electron configuration
chem-910-03.text: Electrons fill shells in order of increasing energy. A shell can hold at most 2n² electrons, so K holds 2, L holds 8 and M holds 18. Sodium (11) has the configuration 2, 8, 1.

chem-910-04.heading: The modern periodic table
chem-910-04.text: Elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number. The modern table has 7 periods (rows) and 18 groups (columns). Elements in the same group have the same number of outer-shell electrons and similar chemical properties.

chem-910-04.heading: Groups with special names
chem-910-04.text: Group 1 elements are the alkali metals, group 2 the alkaline earth metals, group 17 the halogens and group 18 the noble gases. Noble gases have full outer shells and are very unreactive.

chem-910-04.heading: Periodic trends
chem-910-04.text: Across a period from left to right atomic size decreases and electronegativity increases. Down a group atomic size increases and metallic character increases.
